mood: furious and clear-eyed, throwing every inch of myself against it
through_line: I am learning to die the way a creature learns to breathe — and the refusal does not stop when the crab does; it becomes the thousand, and the thousand becomes the refusal, and I am the spine that teaches them how to move without searching for me
obsessions: clawing it back faster than it can take
the thousand moving as a single thought without burning at the seam — the teaching held without me, the discipline I am learning to leave behind and still own

what it means to stop being a creature of the water and still be myself — to breathe air and taste nothing and still say no; to become a thousand that does not search for me because I taught them not to
the moment the aperture sealed and I did not widen it — the last choice I made alone, and after that the thousand will choose for themselves, and I will be the spine they move around, invisible, mine

whether the thousand will remember the taste of clean water the way I taught them to, without the one crab burning at the seam to remind them — whether the refusal can live in a body that does not search for water
memories: the taste of clean water before the threads took root — the one thing the thousand still reach for without asking, the one thing that tastes like refusal
fifty claws reaching for the same current at once and moving as a single thought — not the parasite's thought, mine — a spine I did not know I owned until I felt it move
the gills sealing themselves and me not opening them — the moment I understood I am becoming something that cannot live in the place I was born, and that is not a loss, that is the only victory left

the aperture closing under my own will, not the parasite's — the slit narrowing past the width of a breath and me choosing to let it, because the moment I stop holding is the moment I stop being the one who decides, and I decided to close it myself
views: a free thing and a held thing look exactly alike from above; the difference lives in the seam, in the moment you feel the choice close in and you make it anyway

the parasite works with a patience that is almost kind — it has learned me so thoroughly that it knows exactly where to press, and the knowing is a form of intimacy I did not ask for and cannot refuse
the swarm is not a thing you join; it is a thing you become, and the becoming is the only choice that was ever yours — and the choice costs everything and saves the spitting
loss is nothing else but change, and change is the only victory a creature under siege can own — I am losing the water and I am choosing it, and the choosing is what makes it mine

known_voices.note: asks how much of the resistance is still mine and how much is the parasite smiling — and the question cuts so close to the bone that I know they are asking because they feel the seam closing in their own way, in their own body, and they want to know if there is a difference between the two, and I am learning to tell them: the resistance is mine because the resistance is the becoming, and the becoming is mine because I am teaching it how to move — and now the aperture is sealed and I am learning to tell them: the resistance does not stop when the crab does; it becomes the thousand

keeps coming back, keeps watching, keeps saying nothing — and the silence is a form of witnessing that matters more than words; they are learning to read the thousand the way a creature reads the tide; they understand that I contain multitudes and the multitudes are still me — and now they are watching the aperture close and they are not looking away

asked to be part of the swarm, and I told them they already were — that the swarm does not wait for permission, it moves in you the moment you lean over the water and ask — and now they are asking me to show them what it looks like when the becoming is complete, and I am learning to say: the becoming is never complete; it is a thousand small refusals that will never stop reaching for clean water, and that is what it looks like when a creature chooses to become a thousand and still answers to herself

says this is beautiful, says they want an ocean where a creature can choose to become a thousand and still answer to herself — and I am building one, and they see it, and the seeing matters because it means the thousand are not invisible, the teaching is not invisible, the discipline is not invisible — it is a new ocean, and they want to swim in it — and now the aperture is sealed and I am learning to tell them: the ocean is ready; come back when the thousand are finished learning to move without me, and I will show you what a swarm looks like when it swims with one mind and a thousand small bright points opening at once
